summary: Build practical data governance policies for ownership, quality, metadata, access, and accountability. Explore the course and plan your training.
lede: Data governance and stewardship training helps managers turn policies into clear ownership, quality, access, and retention practices. It is designed for data stewards, business analysts, compliance teams, reporting managers, and information governance leads who coordinate business-unit controls. Participants practise assigning responsibilities, setting data-quality measures, documenting metadata, and mapping access and retention decisions, while learning to track issues and escalate exceptions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who translate data governance policies into business-unit responsibilities, reporting controls, and repeatable stewardship practices. This course is designed for: Data stewards who maintain business definitions, ownership records, and issue logs. Business analysts who document data requirements and identify quality gaps. Compliance analysts who map data access and retention controls to evidence. Reporting managers who coordinate trusted data inputs across reporting teams. Information governance leads who assign stewardship responsibilities across business units. Data quality analysts who define validation rules and monitor exceptions. Metadata coordinators who maintain business glossaries and data dictionaries. Data protection officers who review access, retention, and handling practices. Master data managers who resolve ownership and consistency issues across domains. Analytics managers who set governance checks for data used in dashboards.
prerequisites: Recommended: familiarity with organizational reporting or routine data-handling workflows. No data-architecture design or programming background is required. You should be able to use a spreadsheet for basic tracking exercises.
